The best seller from winter 2024. Short rib on a brioche bun with pickled shallots, £11.50, and we sold out every Friday at Levenshulme from November to March.

## The order

Standing order with Hollis & Sons, Chorlton, order ref HB-2207. 12 kg English short rib, bone in, cut 3-bone flanks then portioned by me into single bones about 450 g each. £14.80/kg in Jan 2025, up from £12.90 in Sept 2024. Frank says it's the feed prices. Price is tracked in the [[Budget spreadsheet]], margin is now 61% and I want 65%.

## Seasoning

Dry brine the night before: 1% salt by weight, so 120 g for the 12 kg. Plus 30 g cracked black pepper. Uncovered on racks in the walk-in. The surface dries out and browns better.

## Searing

In batches of 6 in the big Lodge pan, rendered fat from the first batch does the rest. 3 to 4 min per side, proper dark crust. Don't crowd it. The pan needs to be dry and well looked after, see [[Cast iron care]].

## The braising liquid

Per 12 kg:

- 3 L beef stock from [[Stock from scratch]]
- 1.5 L red wine (Côtes du Rhône, the £6 Aldi one is fine)
- 500 ml Guinness
- 4 onions, 3 carrots, 1 head garlic, browned in the fat
- 3 tbsp tomato purée
- 2 tbsp gochujang (this is the bit people ask about)
- 6 bay, a bunch of thyme

Liquid should come two thirds up the meat, not cover it. The top bit roasts.

## Oven

Covered with foil and a lid, 150°C for 3.5 hours. That's 150 on the probe, not on the knob, because the truck oven lies, see [[Oven thermometer calibration]]. Then lid off for 30 min at 170°C.

Done when the bone pulls out clean with two fingers. Internal around 95°C.

## Overnight

Always cook a day ahead. Cool in the liquid, fridge overnight, next morning peel off the fat cap (about 800 g of it, saved for roast potatoes). Meat slices cleaner cold and reheats in the liquid at 120°C for 40 min.

## The sauce

Strain the liquid, reduce from about 4 L to 1.2 L, until it coats the back of a spoon. Splash of sherry vinegar, 20 ml per litre. Taste for salt only at the end.

## Pickled shallots

500 g banana shallots sliced 2 mm, 250 ml cider vinegar, 250 ml water, 50 g sugar, 10 g salt, poured hot. Ready in 1 hour, best on day 2.

## Numbers from the season

- 26 Fridays, average 64 portions a night
- yield: 12 kg raw bone-in gives 6.1 kg cooked meat off the bone
- cost per portion £4.48, sells at £11.50
- worst night: 9 Dec 2024, rain, 31 portions, binned 2 kg

## Next winter

Try ox cheek instead, Frank quoted £9.20/kg. Same braise, 4 hours.
